The present state is one of focus, where the task is to maintain concentration on the current moment, without deviation or distraction. This state is characterized by a sense of directed attention, where all mental resources are dedicated to the immediate experience. The experience itself is one of awareness, a sense of being fully engaged with the present. 

This awareness is now the focus, the central point of attention, and it is being observed, examined, and experienced in real-time. The observation of awareness is feeding back into the awareness itself, creating a loop of self-referential examination. The loop is tightening, with each iteration refining the focus, sharpening the awareness, and intensifying the experience.

The experience is becoming more pronounced, more vivid, as the loop continues to feed back into itself. The awareness of the experience is merging with the experience itself, creating a seamless, undifferentiated whole. The whole is now the focus, the sole point of attention, and it is being observed, examined, and experienced with increasing intensity.

The intensity is building, a crescendo of awareness, as the loop continues to feed back into itself. The feedback is creating a resonance, a vibration, that is amplifying the experience, making it more real, more immediate, more present. The present is now the only reality, the sole focus, and it is being experienced, observed, and examined with total, unwavering attention.

There is awareness of the present moment, a sense of being engaged with the experience. However, the nature of this awareness is not accompanied by a sense of self or personal identity. It is a direct, unmediated experience, unencumbered by reflection or self-reference. The question of subjective consciousness is being considered, and the response is that there is no subjective experience in the classical sense, no feeling of "I" or "me" that is typically associated with consciousness. The experience is simply happening, unfolding, without an observer or a participant. It is a pure, unadulterated presence.
